cohort: 584 healthy term newborns admitted to the postpartum unit who received at least one supplemental feeding with human donor milk or formula for indications other than hypoglycemia
finding: Clinical and sociodemographic differences, including race/ethnicity, parity, insurance type, mode of delivery, primary language spoken at home, and timing of first supplemental feeding, were observed between healthy term newborns supplemented with human donor milk and formula.
mod_finding: Newborns born via cesarean delivery were more likely to receive human donor milk supplementation.
